title: Graduate Research Fellow
description_1: Sole evaluator on an independent, IRB-approved mixed-methods needs and access-barriers evaluation among immigrant men age 55+ - why faith-based community spaces are trusted and used while public libraries and recreation centers are not.
description_2: Developed the logic model, evaluation plan, IRB protocol, and every data collection instrument, then fielded 26 surveys and 16 semi-structured interviews - all instruments built in both English and Spanish.
description_3: Led all data collection, cleaning, and quality assurance; analyzed quantitative data in R (descriptive and correlation statistics) and coded interview transcripts, isolating awareness, language, privacy, and trust as the operative barriers.
description_4: Built the design on data-equity and community-based principles, including a participatory visual-mapping activity in which participants marked the places they trusted, avoided, or could not reach rather than selecting from predetermined categories.
description_5: Translated findings into a policy brief with actionable outreach and facility-design recommendations; presented to the ASU Watts College board and reported to AmeriCorps and community partners. Brief selected for publication in an edited volume.

title: Service-Demand Evaluation - Public Affairs Capstone
institution: Lake Havasu City Police Department / ASU (PAF 509)
description_1: Primary evaluator for a municipal client that sets patrol staffing by resident ratio while absorbing roughly 1.6 million annual visitors against 62,400 residents, and logged 50,493 calls for service in 2025.
description_2: Grounded the design in a systematic review of workload-staffing literature and U.S. Department of Justice COPS Office guidance; 13-source review spanning criminology, operations research, economics, and tourism management.
description_3: Obtained 44 months of record-level administrative data (January 2023 - August 2026) through a public records request and built an extraction, cleaning, and validation pipeline in R, converting 44 monthly PDF files into one analysis-ready dataset.
description_4: Analyzing monthly demand for seasonal structure and priority mix, and benchmarking against peer municipalities with comparable seasonal swings.
description_5: Deliverable is a client-facing report with costed three-to-five year and ten-year staffing options, visualized for decision-makers without technical background.

title: Power Hour: Making Minutes Count - Evaluation Design
